results.title: What is Runway Width? | TarmacView
results.content:
Runway width, often referred to as the lateral dimension of a runway, is a foundational parameter in airport planning, engineering, and daily operations. Unlike runway length (which is associated with takeoff and landing performance), runway width ensures lateral safety margins for aircraft ground handling, crosswind operations, and the effective placement of markings and lighting. Correctly designed runway width is essential for safe, efficient, and future-proof airport infrastructure. [...] How is runway width defined in airport design?
:   Runway width is the straight-line, perpendicular distance between the edges of the prepared, load-bearing surface of a runway. It excludes shoulders, blast pads, and safety areas, focusing solely on the pavement or surface designed for aircraft movement. This dimension is a critical safety and operational parameter, determined by the largest, most demanding aircraft expected to use the runway regularly. [...] Definition

LaGuardia Airport (LGA) in New York operates three runways that support a dense mix of commercial, cargo, and general aviation operations. Runway length at LGA is constrained by its nearby airspace, urban setting, and the East River shoreline. Understanding the exact dimensions and layout helps explain performance limits for different aircraft types and why certain operations are restricted compared with larger outlying airports. [...] When evaluated against other New York metropolitan airports, LaGuardia’s runway length is intermediate between smaller general aviation fields and the longest runways at JFK. John F. Kennedy International offers runways exceeding 13,000 feet, supporting very heavy long-haul operations with higher performance margins. Newark Liberty has runways around 11,000 feet, giving it flexibility for a wide range of aircraft in varied weather. LGA is designed for short- to medium-haul operations where [...] ## Future Outlook and Modernization

Ongoing airspace redesign and terminal modernization at LaGuardia focus on improving flows rather than extending runways. NextGen navigation allows more precise routing, which helps optimize the use of existing runway length. While physical extensions are unlikely due to cost and geography, procedural improvements continue to enhance capacity and maintain safety margins for the wide variety of aircraft that use the airport.
